limited_overlap.description: 894 of 12000 training applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their median prior earnings are 77,185 dollars. Their effects are extrapolated from the other applicants.
180 of 4000 new applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their predicted effects rest on extrapolation.

warnings: Follow-up survey response: 10006 of 12000 applicants answered (83.4%). Response depends on enrolment (logit coefficient 0.42 per enrolment). Results assume response is random given the covariates and enrolment; nothing in the data tests this, and response that depends on unobserved earnings would bias every estimate.
Final model: linear. RScorer (held-out responders): linear=-0.0007, causal_forest=-0.0020.

Instrument check: distance_km first-stage t statistic given covariates = -7.7; its direct t statistic in the follow-up earnings regression = -1.99. Distance-based IV estimate of the ATE = 12715 (90% -2211 to 27640).

Conditional-on-employment earnings effect = 3651 (90% 2809 to 4492); this compares employed applicants only, so it is not a causal effect on earnings of the employed unless employment is unaffected by enrolment.

Omitted-confounder benchmark: ATE when each strong confounder is dropped from the adjustment set: without prior_earnings = -4537, without months_unemployed = 2581, without education = 2296; full model = 2680.
Run time 10 seconds with seed 1; training rows 12000, responders 10006.
